messages.content: Quick Santa Fe update. My wife doesn't want to gamble on the SAF connection, so treat Albuquerque as the plan. If we use the later SFO-ABQ nonstop with assigned seats instead of the earlier OAK option, does the drive still leave a normal dinner window? Also compare Inn of the Governors prepaid versus the Railyard hotel with easier cancellation.

Rechecked May 16-19. SFO-ABQ nonstop is 3:10-6:34 p.m.; OAK nonstop is about 45 minutes earlier but no assigned seats. With SFO, carry-ons and a rental counter put you on I-25 around 7:05, at the hotel around 8:15-8:30. That's workable if dinner is near the hotel or reserved for 8:30/8:45. The SAF via Denver still has a tight connection and a later arrival, so I would not move back to it.
We can leave after lunch but not much earlier. Is that I-25 drive okay at dusk?

Yes. It is mostly straightforward interstate, about 60-70 minutes in normal traffic. It is not a mountain-road drive. I would keep the first-night dinner close to the Railyard/Guadalupe area rather than trying to park twice around the Plaza.
Hotel rate trade-off?

Inn of the Governors: about $319 prepaid, strong historic Plaza feel, breakfast, Del Charro on site, guest rating around 4.4, parking included but tighter. Trade-off is the nonrefundable rate and older-room feel. Railyard District Hotel: about $286 on a flexible rate, guest rating around 4.5, newer room style, cancellation until May 13, self-parking about $18/night. Trade-off is less old-Santa-Fe atmosphere and a 12-15 minute walk to the Plaza.
For this weekend, room basics don't matter much. Walkability and a place to sit after dinner matter more.

Then the Railyard hotel is the better fit. You have Tomasita's, Cafecito, Second Street Brewery, and casual patio/lobby seating nearby, and you can leave the car parked. Inn of the Governors is the historic upgrade if you want the Plaza right outside the door, but the prepaid term is the problem.
Parking at the Inn isn't actually easier?
Not really. It may be included, but the lot is tighter and first-come. The Railyard option has paid self-parking in an adjacent lot with in-out access, which is simpler after arriving late from ABQ.
Okay. Hold SFO-ABQ and the Railyard hotel as the planned version. SAF only if fares drop a lot. Still no booking.

Saved, not booked: Friday May 16 SFO-ABQ afternoon nonstop, rental-car drive to Santa Fe with dinner planned near the Railyard; Railyard District Hotel May 16-19 on the flexible rate; Monday ABQ return after lunch; Inn of the Governors as the historic upgrade only, and SAF via Denver only if the fare gap narrows enough to justify the connection risk. Before booking I will recheck seat-together availability, parking cost, and cancellation terms.

messages.content: New one: Kansas City/Olathe municipal utility visit. I need to be at the wastewater facility Tuesday June 10 around 7:15 for safety processing, then I have a distributor lunch-and-learn Wednesday in Overland Park. They might add a short debrief Wednesday afternoon, so don't lock the return yet. Can you build flight and hotel options into MCI?
Yes. Which Bay Area airports are fair game, and how late is too late to land Monday with that Tuesday start? Also any hotel radius or rate ceiling?

SFO, OAK, or SJC are all fine if the routing is clean. I don't want to land after 8:30 p.m. Monday. Hotel should be Olathe or southern Overland Park, decent ratings, parking, coffee/fridge if available, and something easy for dinner nearby. Keep it practical, not downtown.

For Monday June 9 into MCI, three workable choices stand out. Best schedule: Southwest OAK-MCI nonstop about 1:25-6:45 p.m.; cleanest routing and you can reach Olathe before 8:30. United option: SFO-DEN-MCI around 12:40-7:55 with a 70-minute Denver connection; assigned seats, but one more failure point. Acceptable backup: Delta SFO-SLC-MCI around 11:20-6:35; good arrival, but it pulls you out before lunch. I would not use the late SFO-SEA-MCI options for a 7:15 site check-in.
OAK is fine if it's really nonstop. The United connection is tempting only if the timing is safer. Is Denver short?

The United connection is not unsafe, but it is less forgiving: about 65-70 minutes in Denver, and the MCI arrival is a little before 8. With a rental-car pickup and a 30-35 minute drive south, hotel arrival is closer to 9. The OAK nonstop is the better fit for protecting Tuesday morning unless the fare jumps or the nonstop disappears.
Use OAK as planned for outbound, then. What about coming home if the debrief runs to 4:30 Wednesday?

A 4:30 p.m. finish in Overland Park makes most Wednesday returns tight. You are roughly 40-50 minutes from MCI before rental return and security. A 6:10 p.m. nonstop works only if you are released by about 3:00. A later one-stop exists around 7:45-8:10, but it gets you back near or after midnight. Cleaner plan: keep Thursday morning as the practical return until the client confirms the debrief.
Show both, but don't book the return yet.

Return shortlist: Wednesday best case is MCI-OAK nonstop about 6:10-8:05 p.m.; requires leaving the distributor area around 3:00. Wednesday backup is MCI-DEN-SFO around 7:50 p.m. with a late Bay Area arrival; acceptable only if you want to avoid another hotel night. Thursday practical return is MCI-OAK nonstop around 10:35 a.m.-12:25 p.m., or United MCI-DEN-SFO around 9:15 a.m.-1:10 p.m. if SFO is easier that day.
Hotel options next. I care more about Tuesday access than being near downtown restaurants.

Shortlist near Olathe/south Overland Park: Embassy Suites by Hilton Kansas City Olathe, guest rating about 4.5, free parking, in-room fridge and coffee maker, breakfast, on-site bar/restaurant plus nearby dinner, roughly 10-15 minutes to the plant and 15-20 to 119th/Metcalf. Courtyard Kansas City Olathe, rating about 4.6, free parking, coffee maker and mini-fridge, newer/quiet, several restaurants within a short drive, about 10 minutes to the plant; no full breakfast included. Hilton Garden Inn Overland Park, rating about 4.2, free parking, fridge/coffee, on-site restaurant, very convenient for Wednesday but more like 25 minutes to the plant Tuesday.
Least annoying Tuesday morning?

Embassy or Courtyard in Olathe. Embassy is the best fit if you want breakfast and an easy dinner without thinking; Courtyard is the acceptable backup if rate matters or you want newer-room feel. I would put Hilton Garden Inn only if Wednesday becomes the priority.
Rate check. If Embassy is over about 220 before tax, go Courtyard.

Current flexible rates: Embassy about $214 per night before tax, Courtyard about $189, Hilton Garden Inn about $176. Embassy is still under your ceiling and includes breakfast and parking, so its total value is closer than the nightly rate suggests.
Good. Can we structure the hotel so I don't pay for Wednesday night if they release me early?

Yes, but I would avoid one single Monday-through-Thursday reservation. Better structure is Monday and Tuesday nights as the core stay, plus a separate Wednesday-night flexible reservation that can be canceled once the debrief is confirmed. I will check the cutoff; if the Wednesday-night cancellation deadline is earlier than the client can commit, I will ask before booking.
Please save the shortlist. Also draft a quick note to the distributor asking them to confirm the debrief window and any site check-in details.

Saved, no booking. Best-fit outbound is Monday June 9 OAK-MCI nonstop, 1:25-6:45 p.m., rental car to Olathe. Return remains open: Wednesday 6:10 p.m. only if you are released around 3:00; otherwise Thursday morning MCI-OAK or MCI-DEN-SFO. Hotel lead is Embassy Suites Olathe at about $214 before tax with free parking, fridge/coffee, breakfast, and nearby dinner; Courtyard Olathe is the lower-rate backup. Draft note: I am planning travel for the June 10 Olathe facility visit and the June 11 lunch-and-learn. Could you confirm the Tuesday safety check-in address/time, PPE or photo restrictions, and whether the Wednesday debrief is expected to end by 3:00 p.m. or closer to 4:30? That timing determines whether I return Wednesday evening or Thursday morning.
